t: You're standing where the St James's Theatre once stood, in King Street, St James's. It opened in 1835 and was demolished in 1957. It was built for a popular singer, John Braham, but it lost money, and he retired after three seasons. A string of managements failed over the next forty years, and the theatre gained a reputation as an unlucky one. It only began to prosper from 1879 under the actors John Hare and Madge and W. H. Kendal. Its architect was Samuel Beazley, the leading theatre architect of his time.
